subject: Request: Dedicated pool backfill grace window and queueing allowance
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@auroratech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@auroratech.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool backfill: request for short grace window

Hi Irene,

Quick context: our nightly batch re-index/backfill (heavy KV warm-up job) has been bumping into your reserved GPU pool and causing short spikes in queue times for our low-latency inference workflows. Our infra team can reschedule, but the simplest operational fix for now is to request a short, scheduled "backfill grace window" during which AuroraTech can run those jobs against our dedicated capacity without triggering eviction/preemption for a small bounded period.

Can Redwood approve a 10-minute backfill allowance per night for the next 90 days while we ship a more permanent throttling change? We are flexible on the timing (we propose 03:00–03:30 UTC) and can accept additional observability hooks and pre-notification.

Attached: auroratech_slo_change_request.pdf (high level asks + histogram of recent queueing spikes).

If a short temporary exception isn't feasible, please suggest alternatives — credits, smaller reserved burst windows, or scheduled burst tokens.

Thanks,
Sam Park
Head of Platform Engineering
AuroraTech

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@auroratech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool backfill: request for short grace window

Sam — thanks for the clear description and the attachment. We can definitely discuss options; looping in Karthik for technical behavior and Marissa/Ben for contract/credits side.

Couple quick clarifying Qs before we propose language:
- Is the backfill strictly sequential (single job) or spread across many small workers?
- Do you need the window to be exclusive (no preemption at all) or a throttled/soft-preemption policy where jobs can be slowed but not immediately evicted?
- Are you willing to accept a nightly window up to 15 minutes if that helps avoid repeated scheduling friction?

Karthik / Marissa / Ben — could you weigh in on feasibility, telemetry hooks we should require, and what contract amendment would look like (addendum vs. scheduled maintenance exception)?

Irene Choi
Head of Enterprise Success | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>, Sam Park <sam.park@auroratech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool backfill: request for short grace window

Thanks — technical note from infra/runtime:

Short summary of behavior
- Dedicated pools are designed to prioritize pinned low-latency jobs. Background/backfill jobs that consume GPU can cause queueing when concurrency reaches pool capacity.
- We have two mechanisms to manage this: (1) soft preemption (throttling + fairshare), (2) hard eviction when we must honor strict latency SLOs.

Proposal for a safe temporary window
- Allow a scheduled nightly backfill window of 10 minutes (configurable up to 15) where we apply a "backfill throttle" profile: jobs are admitted but limited to N% GPU slices and prevented from triggering immediate eviction of pinned requests.
- Instrumentation: require a telemetry hook — a nightly JSON post with aggregate queue_time_p50/p95 and token_count for the window. Redwood will also enable an alert if queue_p95 > 200ms during the window.
- Auto-fallback: if the pool sees sustained tail-latency > 400ms for more than 2 minutes, the throttle auto-tightens (reduces admitted backfill concurrency) and we send a page to both teams.

Operational caveats
- This is not strictly "exclusive use" — it is a controlled backfill with enforced caps. It prevents hard evictions but can still increase micro-latency.
- We can implement this immediately as a runtime policy and run it in trial for 30 days. For anything beyond 90 days, we'd suggest a formal SLO amendment.

I can add the runtime knobs to a feature branch and schedule a brief runbook review with your ops team.

— Karthik
Principal, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@auroratech.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool backfill: request for short grace window

Sam — appreciate the flexibility. From a commercial/contract perspective here are the options we typically offer for temporary behavioral exceptions:

1) Timeboxed operational amendment (preferred) — 90-day trial: implement the throttle profile Karthik described, Redwood provides a one-time account credit equal to 10% of one month of reserved capacity if telemetry shows queue_p95 impact within the window. Amendment is a short addendum (SLA schedule) not a full contract renegotiation.

2) Permanent SLO addendum — commit to a nightly backfill allowance in the SLO schedule, with defined limits and additional monitoring/credits. This requires legal signoff and typically a 30-day lead time.

3) Alternative: scheduled burst tokens — AuroraTech buys a small burst-token allocation that Redwood guarantees won't be preempted during the token window. This is usually faster but has different economics.

Attached is a redline snippet for the 90-day operational amendment (redline-proposed-slo-snippet.docx). Ben — can you confirm whether the proposed credit calculation is within our pricing guardrails?

Marissa Cole
Director of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Park <sam.park@auroratech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, AuroraTech Procurement <procurement@auroratech.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool backfill: request for short grace window

Team — thanks, this all looks good. We are happy to proceed with option 1 (90-day timeboxed operational amendment) with the following asks:

- Agree to a 10-minute nightly window (03:00–03:30 UTC slot, we may occasionally shift by up to 30 minutes with 48h notice).
- Require the telemetry post each morning and a weekly summary dashboard for the trial period.
- Accept the 10% one-time credit if telemetry shows p95 within the window increased by more than 20% vs baseline.

Please confirm and send the amendment for signature (DocuSign preferred). Once signed we'll enable the backfill throttle from our side and run the trial.

Sam Park
Head of Platform Engineering
AuroraTech
